payload.title: CLI and MCP parity for scheduling and announcements
payload.description:
Part of the scheduled publishing and announcements epic. Design: docs/plans/scheduled-publishing-and-announcements.md ("CLI and MCP parity").

Goal: everything an editor or owner does in the console (except the browser-only OAuth step) works through the `papyrus` CLI and MCP from one operation table.

Shape: operations `schedule set|change|clear|suggest|list`, `announcements list|show|approve|edit|withdraw|retry|pause|resume`, `announcements settings show|set`, `announcements account status`; console routes call the same table (as `editorial_checks.OPERATIONS`); mutations write unless `--dry-run`; `announcements account connect` prints the console link; secrets are never accepted as CLI arguments.

Depends on: the scheduling backend story and the eligibility story.

```gherkin
Feature: Agents and people at a terminal can schedule and manage announcements
  Our agents work through the CLI and MCP, so every console action has the same
  operation behind it.

  Scenario: Scheduling from the CLI
    When an agent runs "papyrus schedule set <story> --at '2026-11-13 09:00'"
    Then the Story is scheduled for 09:00 in the publication's time zone
    And the console shows the same schedule

  Scenario: A dry run changes nothing
    When an agent runs "papyrus announcements approve <id> --dry-run"
    Then it prints what would be posted
    And nothing is posted

  Scenario: Connecting needs the browser
    When Ryan runs "papyrus announcements account connect"
    Then the CLI prints the console link for connecting

  Scenario: The same rules everywhere
    Given approval is required on MoM
    When an agent approves a draft that failed its fact check through MCP
    Then it is refused with the same message the console shows
```

Open questions: none.
